title: Product Manager, Billing (Senior Staff)
description:
Are you ready to unlock intelligence?

If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria below but are still interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box - we’re looking for candidates that are particularly strong in a few areas, and have some interest and capabilities in others.

THE MISSION

Kong is building the future of AI connectivity, empowering developers to connect, secure, and scale their applications with speed and intelligence. We are hiring a Product Manager, Billing to lead the product and systems work behind how Konnect makes money: entitlements, metering, checkout, invoicing, provisioning, and the enterprise and marketplace motions that surround them.

In this role you are the product owner of Konnect's commercial operating layer: the systems that translate what Sales sells and what customers use into what ends up on an invoice. That means plan and entitlement design, the usage metering pipeline, self-serve checkout and subscription lifecycle, customer organization and billing admin experiences, enterprise billing workflows (CPQ sync, custom contracts), and cloud marketplace billing. You will work hand-in-hand with Product Growth, Pricing & Packaging, Finance, GTM, Sales, and Engineering.

This role reports to the Sr Director, Product (Platform) and sits at the intersection of two multi-year transformations: Kong's move from a single-product API gateway company into a multi-product enterprise, and Monetization's company-wide overhaul of pricing and packaging. The Billing, Provisioning, and Fulfillment program has historically been manual and relationship-driven. Your job is to turn it into a product, so Sales can sell more, Finance can bill more accurately, and customers get an experience that matches the quality of what they are paying for.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

- Platform Vision: Set a multi-year direction for how Konnect prices, meters, entitles, and invoices. Decide what becomes shared platform capability versus what stays feature-specific, and sequence delivery so near-term work lands without creating long-term drag.

- Unified Entitlements: Build the entitlements model that determines what every customer can access within Konnect. Make entitlements a first-class concept that is consistently defined in contracts, enforced in-product, honored by provisioning, and reflected in billing.

- Pricing & Packaging Delivery: Act as the product and systems counterpart to Monetization. Translate pricing and packaging decisions into production reality: configuring plans, reshaping metering, updating contracts, coordinating customer migrations, and making sure a rollout doesn't disrupt existing revenue.

- Metering & Usage Visibility: Run the event pipeline, aggregation layer, and reporting experiences that show customers what they consumed and what they are being charged. Hold a financial-grade bar on accuracy, auditability, and reconcilability.

- Checkout & Subscription Lifecycle: Own how customers self-serve onto a plan, change plans, renew, lapse, and recover. That covers plan discovery, checkout, the underlying payments integration, subscription state, retries and dunning, and the admin surfaces where customers manage their own billing.

- Enterprise & Marketplace Motions: Connect Kong's enterprise sales and channel motions to the billing stack: CPQ-to-entitlement sync, bespoke contract handling, invoice-based billing, and marketplace billing across AWS, GCP, and Azure as we expand our presence there.

- Fulfillment Automation: Replace today's manual, high-touch provisioning and fulfillment processes with productized, automated workflows. This includes migrating off our current metering and billing system onto a target stack that supports the new pricing and packaging framework.

We combine original research, books, strategic advising, and a modern media engine to reach leaders who are ready to make consequential changes.
Our books are central to that mission. The Science of Scaling is a primary path into our work, and Power Law Strategy is the next major expression of it. We are building a creative team with the intellectual depth of a research firm, the taste of a premium editorial studio, and the accountability of a serious performance business. The Mission
Create performance video that earns the attention and trust of serious entrepreneurs and moves the right people toward Scaling.com . We are building toward at least 40 qualified, attended enrollment calls and 10 or more enrollments per day. Your work helps create the qualified demand behind that goal.
The path is straightforward: a strong idea and credible source material become a persuasive video ad; paid distribution gives us real feedback; that feedback makes the next piece better. What This Role Is

This type of work-work that changes the world-is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

THE ROLE

Our Site Reliability Engineering team owns the reliability, observability and incident management of the internal engineering platform that product teams across Everpure build and run their services on. We define how reliability is measured, operate the shared services the platform depends on, run the incident lifecycle, and remove the operational toil that slows engineering down.

As a Senior Site Reliability Engineer in Prague you will own the reliability of a group of platform services end to end and lead one or more of the programmes that raise reliability across the organisation. You will set technical direction within your area, guide less experienced engineers, and work closely with the product teams whose services run on the platform and with SRE colleagues in our other engineering sites.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Service level objectives and error budgets. Lead the definition of objectives with service owners, design how they are measured and reported, and own the reliability indicators the organisation tracks, including time to detect and time to recover. Use them to shape the team's priorities and to make the case for reliability work with engineering leadership.

• Shared platform services. Own the architecture and operation of the messaging, caching, database and continuous-integration services the platform depends on. Lead their evolution to highly available designs, including redundancy, capacity planning, upgrade strategy and tested recovery procedures.

• Automation. Identify the largest sources of operational toil and lead the engineering work that removes them. Help define how AI is applied to incident triage and remediation, including the safeguards around automated actions, and measure the effect on recovery time.

• Production readiness. Run design and production-readiness reviews for new and changing services, set the reliability expectations product teams are held to, and coach engineers across teams on reliability practices.

• Technical leadership. Mentor engineers on the team, review designs and changes, and represent the team's reliability work with partner teams and leadership.

• Hands-on expertise operating distributed systems on Linux and Kubernetes using Infrastructure as Code and CI/CD pipelines across multi-cloud or hybrid environments.

This type of work-work that changes the world-is what the tech industry was founded on. So, if you're ready to seize the endless opportunities and leave your mark, come join us.

Proposal Tools Analyst

Purpose

The Apollo programme is replacing the many separate tools used at each sales stage with one operating model. In the Proposing stage, that means one new proposal platform that produces a single, standard customer business case. It replaces the self-service tools that today give different answers for the same customer scenario.

The Proposal Tools Analyst lays the groundwork that makes this possible. You will work through the existing business case, TCO, RFX and proposal tools. You'll turn what you learn into one prioritised, traceable set of requirements. Then you'll make sure each old tool is retired safely.

The role has three parts:

• Understand the estate. Work with each tool owner to document what their tool does, what data it relies on, who uses it and why.

• Define the platform. Turn that understanding into one set of system requirements that the build team works and tests against.

• Retire safely. Switch off each old tool only once the new platform has been shown to cover what the field needs from it.

What Success Looks Like

• Every proposal, business case and RFP tool in GSO is known to the programme. Each in-scope tool has a full document that its owner has checked.

• There is one requirements catalogue, kept in sync with the prototype. Every requirement traces back to the field need and the tool it came from.

• Requirements are prioritised with the Field Advisory Group and Proposal Track leads, so the build team works from one ranked list.

• Testing covers the documented requirements, and the Field Advisory Group has formally signed it off.

• Tools are retired on schedule without disrupting the field. Each retirement is signed off against a capability map, not a date.

• There is an agreed recommendation for RFP and RFQ tooling.

What You'll Be Doing

Discovery

• Build on the Apollo dashboard inventory with a detailed document for each tool: scope, functions, users, data, calculation logic, outputs and limits.

• Find tools that aren't recorded yet and get them submitted to the programme.

• Trace each tool's data sources, assumptions and hard-coded values. Flag overlaps, gaps and places where tools give different financial outputs.

Requirements and Product Partnership

• Turn field needs and tool functions into clear, testable requirements, and feed them into the prototype as it changes.

• Decide what to rebuild, retire or combine, and record why.

• Work with Global Value Management to document TCO, cash flow and P&L requirements. Capture non-functional needs too, such as Salesforce write-back, governance, permissions and auditability.

• Work with the Business Platform Owner and DTG as the business-side counterpart. Help shape releases that let old tools be retired as early as possible.

Testing and Decommissioning

• Make sure test scope and test cases map directly to the requirements. Take completed testing to the Field Advisory Group for sign-off.

• Own the capability map that links each old tool to the requirements that must be delivered before it can be switched off.

• Set exit criteria and transition paths with tool owners, and give Sales Enablement what they need for cutover training.

• Capture logic and content worth keeping before a tool is switched off.

RFP Tooling

Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. We're proud to be a Living Wage accredited Employer.

 

What You’ll Do:

CoreWeave’s Physical AI team is building the essential cloud platform for AI innovators, applying machine learning to solve intractable physics and engineering challenges. We operate at the intersection of advanced cloud infrastructure and applied data science, transforming how complex industrial products - such as automotive systems, aircraft, and advanced batteries - are conceived, tested, and developed.

About the role:

As an Applied Researcher, you will help solve machine learning problems across the Physical AI space. This is a hands-on role for someone with a strong technical foundation and a generalist mindset who wants to contribute across problem framing, experimentation, deployment, and ongoing support, with guidance from experienced researchers and engineers.

You will work closely with engineering, product, and client-facing teams to turn advanced ML methods into production-ready solutions that can be trusted in real customer environments. The role blends applied research with practical delivery, and requires someone who can work collaboratively, surface risks and limitations, and communicate technical decisions clearly.

• Experience in data science, machine learning, or applied AI, gained through industry roles, applied research, or a combination of both, with evidence of applying ML to practical problems.

• Strong programming skills in Python, with practical experience using scientific computing and ML libraries such as NumPy, pandas, SciPy, scikit-learn, PyTorch, or TensorFlow.

• Experience contributing to the deployment or support of ML systems, or a good understanding of how models move from experimentation into production, including cloud-based environments.

• Strong grounding in statistical modelling, machine learning experimentation, and evaluation.

• Experience working with time-series, high-dimensional, or imperfect real-world datasets.

• Strong technical curiosity and a habit of keeping up with current ML and AI research.

• Comfortable working cross-functionally with engineering, product, and customer-facing teams, and able to explain technical decisions clearly to different audiences.

Preferred: (if applicable)

• Background in engineering, physics, chemistry, or another STEM discipline connected to complex physical systems.

• Experience with anomaly detection, optimisation, reliability-focused modelling, or related approaches in industrial settings.

• Experience building or experimenting with agents or autonomous systems.

• Familiarity with MLOps, model monitoring, and efficient compute practices.

• Experience working with sparse, noisy, or imperfect real-world data from labs, heavy industry, or other applied environments.

• Track record of collaborating closely with deployed or client-facing teams to bring advanced methods into operational use.

title: Research Intern, Frontier Speculative Decoding (Summer 2027)
description:
About the Role

The Speculative Decoding team at Together AI builds the draft models and algorithms that let large language models generate faster without changing their outputs. Our speculators run in production on frontier open models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and GLM. Our work sits at the intersection of model training, inference algorithms and serving systems, and we co-design all three to lower the cost and latency of generation.

As a research intern, you will dive into open questions in speculative decoding: new drafter architectures and verification schemes, knowledge distillation and training recipes that align draft and target models, and drafters that adapt as traffic shifts. You will train and fine-tune draft models at scale on dedicated GPU clusters, and test your ideas against realistic serving workloads, including long-context and agentic traffic.

Projects aim to answer important research questions in speculative decoding, enabling faster generation on frontier models, drafters that keep pace with changing workloads, and robust, reproducible evaluation under real traffic.

Past Research

Speculative decoding research by Together researchers, interns and academic collaborators includes:

• Speculative Speculative Decoding (ICLR 2026)

• When RL Meets Adaptive Speculative Training: A Unified Training-Serving System (ICML 2026)

• Beat the Long Tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training (MLSys 2026)

Responsibilities

• Research and prototype new efficient speculative decoding algorithms and draft model architectures

• Train, fine-tune and distill draft models, and design rigorous experiments to validate hypotheses.

• Implement optimized version for serving engines to show efficacy in real world workloads

• Communicate the plans, progress, and results of projects to the broader team

• Share findings through technical write-ups and blog posts, and help bring successful ideas into production

Requirements

• Currently pursuing a Master's or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field

• Strong knowledge of Machine Learning and Deep Learning fundamentals

• Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning large models with distributed training frameworks (e.g., Megatron-LM, FSDP)

• Familiarity with modern model architectures, such as Mixture-of-Experts and hybrid attention

Preferred Qualifications

• Prior research experience in speculative decoding, efficient inference, or efficient machine learning

• Publications at leading conferences in machine learning or systems (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, MLSys)

• Experience with knowledge distillation, post-training, or reinforcement learning

• Familiarity with LLM serving engines (e.g., vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM)

• Contributions to open-source machine learning projects

About Together AI

Together AI, the AI Native Cloud, is purpose-built for AI engineers. AI application developers get high-performance inference that scales reliably, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning for creating frontier-level specialized models, and pre-training at massive scale for fully custom intelligence, all around a marketplace of leading open models that teams can run, adapt, and own. Trusted by Cursor, Decagon, ElevenLabs, Salesforce, and Zoom, Together serves 400+ trillion tokens a month.

Our internship program runs 12 to 14 weeks, giving you the opportunity to work alongside industry-leading engineers and researchers across multiple teams. This cohort's internship dates span May 17th to August 6th or June 14th to September 3rd.

Compensation

We offer competitive compensation, housing stipends, and other competitive benefits. The estimated US hourly rate for this role is $58 - $70 an hour. title: Swahili Language Linguist & Original Puzzle Designer
description:
We are recruiting highly skilled linguists and creative thinkers for an exclusive content development project. Our goal is to evaluate and push the boundaries of advanced linguistic and reasoning capabilities by creating original, highly complex reasoning puzzles in various target languages. These puzzles must be solvable by a smart, educated native speaker, but resistant to standard automated solving techniques or web searches.
As a Puzzle Designer, you will write original reasoning prompts in your native language. You will focus on deep structural, cultural, and logical nuances that only a true native speaker can navigate.
You will create puzzles across three primary categories:

• Linguistic Reasoning: Puzzles based on complex grammar rules, syntactic structures, or linguistic ambiguities unique to your language.

• Cultural Reasoning: Logic puzzles grounded in deep cultural context, local traditions, or culturally-grounded mathematics that AI lacks the lived experience to understand.

• Wordplay & Riddles: Advanced, original riddles, puns, or double-meanings that do not exist on the internet and cannot be easily translated word-for-word.

Deliverables per item:
For every puzzle you create, you will be required to submit the following:

• Native-Language Prompt: The original puzzle written flawlessly in the target language.

• Gold Answer: The definitive, correct solution.

• Rationale: A logical breakdown of why the answer is correct and how a native speaker arrives at it.

• English Translation: A high-quality English translation of the prompt, answer, and rationale for project managers to review.

• Difficulty Rating: An assessment of how challenging the puzzle is for a native speaker.

Who We Are Looking For

• Native-level fluency in the target language with exceptional writing skills.

• High proficiency in English to provide clear, accurate translations and rationales.

• Background in Linguistics, Creative Writing, Translation, or Logic/Mathematics: You understand the mechanics of your language deeply.

• Creative & Analytical Thinker: You can design problems that require lateral thinking, cultural context, and multi-step reasoning rather than memorized facts.

• Advanced Problem-Solving Awareness: You understand how automated and computational systems process language, enabling you to design highly resistant, complex prompts.

What to Avoid (Disqualifiers)

• Trivia questions or historical facts that can be Googled.

• Translating existing English riddles or math problems into your native language.

• Copying puzzles from books, websites, or existing online databases.

About the Role
As a Senior UX/CX Designer , you’ll join our client’s U.S.-based Experience Strategy & Design Studio. It’s a small, horizontally structured team that brings strategy, design, and research together around customer experience. The team is building an internal AI experiences hub for about 10,000 enterprise users. You’ll design end-to-end experiences for it, from early concepts to working prototypes.
The team uses user-centered design as its core methodology, so you’ll already know it well. You’ll work in a fast, iterative environment with direct executive engagement, and you’ll partner with stakeholders across the organization. Success here means taking an ambiguous problem, setting a clear design direction, and delivering work at the level your portfolio shows, with minimal oversight.

• Design end-to-end experiences for internal AI tools, from early concepts and task flows to high-fidelity, working prototypes

Let us walk you through the next steps.
Step 1 - Complete Your Application
Fill in our application form and upload your CV. This stores your profile in our Applicant Tracking System (ATS) and places you into our active job pipelines, making it easier for us to match you with current and future opportunities.
Step 2 - The First Look (One-Way Video Interview)
This is where your application comes to life. We review your CV and video interview to get a feel for your experience, communication style, and overall fit. If we like what we see, you're on to the next step!
Why do we ask for a video?
Because a résumé can tell us what you've done, but it can't show us you . Your video is your moment to shine, and it helps us see:

• How you communicate and connect with people.

• How you present yourself professionally.

• Other opportunities you might be an even better fit for (bonus surprises!).

Think of it as your personal trailer. One great video means we can pitch you for multiple roles and get you in front of the right employers, faster.
Heads up: Some clients watch your video directly, so make it one you'd be proud to have represent you. This is your highlight reel-make it count!
Step 3 - Let's Actually Talk
A Recruitment Specialist calls to chat about your experience, your availability, what you want to earn, and the role itself. Consider it a friendly vibe check.
Step 4 - The Fine Print, Made Fun
We break down what it's like working as an independent contractor-hours, pay, contract terms, the whole deal. No surprises, no fine-print sneakiness. You'll get it all in writing.
Step 5 - Matchmaking Time
Our Talent Delivery Team plays cupid, matching you to clients where you're most likely to shine. We can't promise everyone gets picked, but we're rooting for you.
Step 6 - Showtime
Got shortlisted? We'll set up your interview, prep you like a pro, and have your back the whole way-with a Reworks teammate right there facilitating.
Step 7 - The Verdict
We chase feedback the second it lands and keep you in the loop.

title: Software Engineer, Infrastructure Modelling
description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.

We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

HOW WE OPERATE

- Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

- Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

- Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

- Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

- Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

ROLE SCOPE

- Build the software behind the infrastructure model: services, APIs, and pipelines making the design data programmable.

- Ship generative tooling: layouts, routings, and configurations produced from rules and the model, not manual drafting.

- Integrate the design stack: CAD and BIM platforms, PLM, and the company's data layer speaking one language.

- Own the model data at scale: versioning, validation, and queryability across gigawatts of design.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c.

- You've shipped automation that replaced manual design work.

- You handle geometric and graph-shaped data competently.

- You write production code and integrate messy vendor APIs.

- You work embedded with engineers as your users.

- Bonus: Revit, Tekla, or Forge APIs. IFC toolchains. Computational geometry. Rust, C#, TypeScript, or Python.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

title: Senior Systems / Rust Engineer
description: Blockrotate| Senior Systems / Rust Engineer | Remote (US/EU timezones preferred) | Full-time | $130k - $170k + Equity Blockrotate ( https://blockrotate.com ) builds low-latency copy-trading and execution infrastructure for Polymarket and prediction markets. Copy trading on prediction markets has strange market microstructure. Unlike deep perp DEXes (Binance, Hyperliquid), Polymarket orderbooks are bounded, often thin, and subject to severe adverse selection. When a high-volume leader buys, the book moves immediately. If followers lag by a few hundred milliseconds, or if a platform taxes every order with a 50bps fee, follower alpha drops to zero. Most existing tools in this space either hit users with high per-trade taker fees or ask them to export and paste their master private key into a database. We took a different approach: isolated per-bot deposit wallets (non-custodial via EIP-1967/1271 proxies) and co-located autonomous Rust workers running delta-sync loops directly against the Polymarket CLOB. Stack: - Backend: Rust, Tokio, Axum, Protobuf over WebSockets, SQLite (WAL mode) - Trading Engine: Custom Polymarket CLOB & Data API clients, EIP-712 signing, dynamic slippage ladders, momentum filters, circuit breakers - Frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS What you’d actually work on: - Squeezing latency out of the execution hot path (delta position calculation, order placement, nonce handling, fill verification). - Building better execution protection: momentum filters to dodge toxic order flow, fill stabilization windows, and handling thin book liquidity without moving the market against yourself. - Scaling worker orchestration: our C2 server talks Protobuf to distributed bot workers with monotonic sequence IDs and autonomous reconnect failover. As bot volume scales, we need to keep state reconciliation bulletproof. - Investigating and exploiting prediction market quirks (rebate structures, orderbook snapshotting, MEV/relayer bottlenecks). What we look for: - Strong async Rust experience (Tokio, concurrency, practical memory management). - Experience dealing with websockets, exchange orderbooks, or trading infrastructure shoot an email to jobs@blockrotate.com and tell us why you would be a good fit for us.

title: Staff Data Platform Engineer
description:
Who We Are
At Murmuration , we believe that America's promise is shaped and reshaped by the best ideas and ideals of its communities, and the dreams of the people who believe in a better life for themselves, their families, and each other.
We help organizations build power in their communities in four key ways: we organize a network of values-aligned partners; we provide deep, data-driven insights into people, places, and perspectives; we develop tools that make organizing and engagement easy and more effective; and we offer services that strengthen our partners' capacity to lead change in their communities.
We envision an America where every community has what it needs to help people lead healthy,
free, and dignified lives. We work to redesign the systems and structures we all depend on - how we learn, live, govern, and solve problems - so that they are just, equitable, resilient, and rooted in shared responsibility. By strengthening the ties that hold communities together, we aim for civic life defined by collective action and care, with effective leadership that truly represents everyone.
We are a collaborative, curious, and creative team of organizers, scientists, teachers, technologists, campaign veterans, and more who share the unwavering belief that we can use our gifts in service of transforming America - together.
We've built our team guided by the belief that the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. And so we support each other relentlessly - rallying together to face challenges the same way we celebrate each other's wins.
About the Position
We are seeking a Staff Data Platform Engineer to build opinionated paved roads across engineering.
Murmuration builds technology that helps our partner organizations strengthen civic engagement and organize more effectively in their communities. Our products weave together engagement, outreach, demographic, and voter data with intuitive applications that help partners better understand and act within the communities they serve. Our team is intentionally multidisciplinary and partner-focused. We succeed together by aligning planning, execution, and learning across engineering, product, design, research, data, and partner success. We build complex, data-driven systems that need to work reliably during critical moments, scale as our partners grow, and remain understandable and maintainable as communities and their needs evolve.
Murmuration needs a Staff Data Platform Engineer who improves how teams provision, secure, monitor, troubleshoot, and operate production data systems. The role is hands-on, but its larger purpose is leverage: reusable infrastructure, better defaults, clearer playbooks, and stronger operational visibility. This Staff role oversees operational efficiency: tuning, right-sizing, and choosing data stores.
The Staff Data Platform Engineer is one of the key subject matter experts for datastores. The expertise includes designing, deploying, optimizing, securing, and maintaining databases in the cloud. Each team owns its own data stores, architecture, and access patterns, and you’ll help shape how those choices get made. Your scope will be both wide across teams, stacks, and technologies, as well as deep with a team and solution as required.
This role is suited for a deeply experienced individual contributor whose technical judgment and engineering rigor raises the quality of deliverables across the entire organization. You excel in settings where product priorities and direction can shift rapidly. Your commitment to building inclusive, high-trust, and high-performing teams is visible across the technology organization. And you believe, like we do, that how we build is just as important as what we build.
Job Level: P5
What You’ll Do
As a Staff Data Platform Engineer, you will work across all engineering teams and report to one of our Directors of Software Engineering. You will define guidelines and processes for data access and storage, champion best practices

title: Fraud Operations Analyst
description:
About the Role:

Sezzle is seeking a Fraud Operations Analyst to support fraud monitoring. As part of optimizing the online shopping experience, Sezzle constantly monitors users and transactions for abusive or fraudulent behavior. Our Fraud Operations team reviews suspicious activity flagged by Sezzle’s fraud detection system or escalated from Customer Support agents. Fraud Operations Analysts will block users deemed fraudulent or risky, and clear false positive flags from our automated systems and support agents. We monitor for new trends in fraudulent behavior and continuously evolve our policies and procedures to stay one step ahead. We are looking for a teammate who can work one of the shifts listed below full-time:

• Monday - Friday between 3:00 PM - 11:30 PM Central Time.

This will be a non-exempt/hourly position.

Compensation:

$2,000 USD per month.

Our Company

Sezzle is a cutting-edge fintech company whose long-standing mission is to financially empower the next generation. Only one in three millennials own a credit card, and the vast majority of millennials possess a subprime credit score or no score at all. To address these problems, Sezzle has built a payment platform that increases purchasing power for consumers by offering interest-free installment plans at online stores. This increase in purchasing power for consumers leads to increased sales and basket sizes for the numerous eCommerce merchants that currently work with Sezzle.

As the first and only B-Corp in the payments space, Sezzle’s goal is to help everyone pursue financial freedom, and to invest in social good and ethical initiatives that shape a better world.

At Sezzle, we’re committed to putting purpose alongside profitability. We work hard to maintain rigorous standards of social and environmental performance, accountability, and transparency to build a better world. The employees at Sezzle lean into significant societal and cultural shifts, ensuring internal and external focus on positive impacts that benefit our community.

Responsibilities:

• Monitor real-time transactions and other customer behaviors flagged for fraud and abuse for manual review.

• Investigate individual transactions using internal policies and review methodologies to determine if the transactions are fraudulent or not.

• Understand our systems and tools; investigate account patterns through data analysis.

• Research fraud and user behavior to contribute to machine learning models, rules and other detection systems.

• Collaborate with analysts, operations specialists, data scientists and engineering to improve our fraud prevention mechanisms, processes and tools.

• Learn and maintain strong domain knowledge of the world of fraud including prevention techniques and technologies.

• Maintain or exceed established service level agreements (SLAs) for timely resolution of queued cases to minimize potential losses.

• Handle escalations from internal and external stakeholders in a professional and efficient manner.

Ideal Skills & Experience:

• Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution

• Minimum 1 year of experience in investigating and resolving fraud incidents

• Experienced in analyzing data and comfortable making impactful decisions in a fast-paced and sometimes ambiguous environment

• Attention to detail and ability to multitask

• Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills

• Strong business judgment and communication skills

• Ability to self-start and work with minimal supervision after training

• Able to work through holidays

• Minimum GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0

• Demonstrated experience working with Claude or equivalent large language model tools is required; candidates must be comfortable leveraging AI to enhance productivity, research, and communication.

Preferred Qualifications

Job Summary:

The Service Operations Associate I is a critical operational role within the Client Service department, responsible for executing the administrative and transactional functions that support the firm’s service delivery. This role is designed to complement the Relationship Manager (RM) function by handling the behind-the-scenes execution that enables a seamless client experience. While not client-facing, the Service Operations Associate I plays a vital role in maintaining operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and service consistency.

This position offers a clear career path to Service Operations Associate II and III, with increasing levels of complexity, ownership, and leadership within the operations function.

About the role

Enterprises are increasingly looking to modernize their data ecosystems, improve the reliability and accessibility of their data, and prepare for AI-driven solutions. Often, the biggest challenges aren't the applications themselves, but the underlying data architecture, integration, and quality needed to support them. Every client environment is different, requiring someone who can quickly diagnose complex data challenges and architect practical solutions that deliver measurable business value.

You will shape how enterprise data becomes usable for analytics, AI-assisted experiences, workflows, and other use cases across client organizations. Supply Chain Specialist
Position Overview
The Supply Chain Specialist is responsible for supplier management, procurement, inventory planning, and supply continuity to support hardware operations and customer fulfillment. This role monitors supplier performance, manages material availability, drives cost optimization, and supports new product introductions (NPI) and product lifecycle activities. The ideal candidate is a proactive, detail-oriented self-starter with strong analytical and problem-solving skills, capable of working independently, taking ownership of responsibilities, and collaborating effectively with internal teams and external suppliers.
This is a remote position based in the Pacific or Central time zone, with 10% travel.
Key Responsibilities

• Server as a primary point of contact for external suppliers and partners to coordinate procurement activities, delivery schedules, and operational requirements.

• Monitor supplier performance against key metrics, including quality, cost, on-time delivery, lead times, and responsiveness. Support supplier scorecards, performance reviews, and corrective action follow-ups.

• Coordinate procurement of hardware appliances, components, accessories, and related services, including purchase order processing, supplier acknowledgments, order tracking, and delivery follow-ups.

• Monitor demand forecasts, inventory levels, replenishment requirements, and supplier capacity to support material availability, minimize shortages, and reduce excess inventory.

• Identify and track material shortages, supply constraints, and delivery delays. Coordinate with suppliers and internal teams to resolve issues and minimize fulfillment disruptions.

• Review supplier pricing, purchase price variances, and procurement costs to identify potential cost savings, cost avoidance, and process improvement opportunities.

• Support supply chain readiness for new product introductions, including component sourcing, bill of materials (BOM) reviews, material availability, supplier coordination, and production ramp-up.

• Coordinate supply chain activities related to new SKU setup, engineering changes, product revisions, end-of-sale (EOS), end-of-life (EOL), and component obsolescence.

• Work closely with Sales Operations, Manufacturing, Logistics, Finance, Engineering, and Product Management to support supply chain execution and customer fulfillment requirements.

• Maintain accurate supplier, material, pricing, and procurement records. Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through process standardization, reporting, and automation.

Qualifications

• 5+ years of experience in supply chain management, procurement, or supplier management in a technology or hardware manufacturing environment.

• Experience managing supplier performance, sourcing and purchasing activities, and supply continuity issues.

• Working knowledge of NPI processes, bills of materials, inventory planning, component lead times, and product lifecycle changes.

• Ability to evaluate supplier quotations, negotiate commercial terms, analyze costs, and prioritize competing operational needs.

• Strong analytical, organizational, negotiation, cross-functional communication, and problem-solving skills.

• Excellent written and communication skills

• Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365 applications,
